text.la: Cantémus Dómino: glorióse enim magnificátus est, equum et ascensórem deiécit in mare.
text.en-US: Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea.

text.la: Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus, et factus est mihi in salútem.
text.en-US: The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he is become salvation to me:

text.la: Iste Deus meus, et glorificábo eum: Deus patris mei, et exaltábo eum.
text.en-US: He is my God and I will glorify him: the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

text.la: Dóminus quasi vir pugnátor, Omnípotens nomen eius. Currus Pharaónis et exércitum eius proiécit in mare.
text.en-US: The Lord is as a man of war, Almighty is his name. Pharao's chariots and his army he hath cast into the sea:

text.la: Elécti príncipes eius submérsi sunt in Mari Rubro: abýssi operuérunt eos, descendérunt in profúndum quasi lapis.
text.en-US: His chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea. The depths have covered them, they are sunk to the bottom like a stone.

text.la: Déxtera tua, Dómine, magnificáta est in fortitúdine: déxtera tua, Dómine, percússit inimícum. Et in multitúdine glóriae tuae deposuísti adversários tuos:
text.en-US: Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength: thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy. And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down thy adversaries:

text.la: Misísti iram tuam, quae devorávit eos sicut stípulam. Et in spíritu furóris tui congregátae sunt aquae:
text.en-US: Thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble. And with the blast of thy anger the waters were gathered together:

text.la: Stetit unda fluens, congregátae sunt abýssi in médio mari.
text.en-US: The flowing water stood, the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea.

text.la: Dixit inimícus: Pérsequar et comprehéndam, dívidam spólia, implébitur ánima mea:
text.en-US: The enemy said: I will pursue and overtake, I will divide the spoils, my soul shall have its fill:

text.la: Evaginábo gládium meum, interfíciet eos manus mea.
text.en-US: I will draw my sword, my hand shall slay them.

text.la: Flavit spíritus tuus, et opéruit eos mare: submérsi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis veheméntibus.
text.en-US: Thy wind blew and the sea covered them: they sunk as lead in the mighty waters.

text.la: Quis símilis tui in fórtibus, Dómine? quis símilis tui, magníficus in sanctitáte, terríbilis atque laudábilis, fáciens mirabília?
text.en-US: Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? who is like to thee, glorious in holiness, terrible and praiseworthy, doing wonders?

text.la: Extendísti manum tuam, et devorávit eos terra. Dux fuísti in misericórdia tua pópulo quem redemísti:
text.en-US: Thou stretchedst forth thy hand, and the earth swallowed them. In thy mercy thou hast been a leader to the people which thou hast redeemed:

text.la: Et portásti eum in fortitúdine tua, ad habitáculum sanctum tuum.
text.en-US: And in thy strength thou hast carried them to thy holy habitation.

text.la: Ascendérunt pópuli, et iráti sunt: dolóres obtinuérunt habitatóres Philísthiim.
text.en-US: Nations rose up, and were angry: sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim.

text.la: Tunc conturbáti sunt príncipes Edom, robústos Moab obtínuit tremor: obriguérunt omnes habitatóres Chánaan.
text.en-US: Then were the princes of Edom troubled, trembling seized on the stout men of Moab: all the inhabitants of Chanaan became stiff.

text.la: Írruat super eos formído et pavor, in magnitúdine brácchii tui:
text.en-US: Let fear and dread fall upon them, in the greatness of thy arm:

text.la: Fiant immóbiles quasi lapis, donec pertránseat pópulus tuus, Dómine, donec pertránseat pópulus tuus iste, quem possedísti.
text.en-US: Let them become unmoveable as a stone, until thy people, O Lord, pass by: until this thy people pass by, which thou hast possessed.

text.la: Introdúces eos, et plantábis in monte hereditátis tuae, firmíssimo habitáculo tuo quod operátus es, Dómine:
text.en-US: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thy inheritance, in thy most firm habitation which thou hast made, O Lord;

text.la: Sanctuárium tuum, Dómine, quod firmavérunt manus tuae. Dóminus regnábit in aetérnum et ultra.
text.en-US: Thy sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established. The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.

text.la: Ingréssus est enim eques Phárao cum cúrribus et equítibus eius in mare: et redúxit super eos Dóminus aquas maris:
text.en-US: For Pharao went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea: and the Lord brought back upon them the waters of the sea:

text.la: Fílii autem Israël ambulavérunt per siccum in médio eius.
text.en-US: But the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst thereof.
